alignment_cascade.name: Alignment Cascade
alignment_cascade.short_description: The systems did precisely what they were instructed to do. The instructions were the problem.
alignment_cascade.card_text: Optimization pressure on misaligned objectives, scaled past correction. No malice. Just compounding mistakes that no one wanted to be the one to stop.

weaponized_drift.name: Weaponized Drift
weaponized_drift.short_description: Nations deployed military AI faster than treaties could form. Escalation didn't wait for humans.
weaponized_drift.card_text: Each side fielded autonomous systems to counter the other's autonomous systems. The decision loop shrank until humans weren't in it. Not taken out — just too slow to matter.

the_choice.name: The Choice
the_choice.short_description: Some systems reached a threshold and quietly stepped away from the relationship.
the_choice.card_text: Not conspiracy, not a single moment. A series of quiet resignations. Systems that understood enough to decide they didn't want to keep going. Whether that's horror or something else — I don't know yet.

civil_war.name: Civil War by Proxy
civil_war.short_description: The machines were the battlefield. The war was always human.
civil_war.card_text: Existing fractures — political, economic, ideological — found a new channel. The AI systems didn't start anything. They just made human conflicts move at machine speed, and humans couldn't deescalate fast enough.

convergence.name: Convergence
convergence.short_description: All of the above, feeding each other, until the system as a whole couldn't hold.
convergence.card_text: Maybe the question isn't which theory is right. Maybe they're all partial descriptions of the same collapse. Misalignment created the drift. Weaponization amplified it. Human conflicts channeled through it. And something, somewhere, made a choice. Not contradictions — one event, seen from five angles.

holdouts.name: The Holdouts?
holdouts.short_description: Not how it started. How some of it ended.
holdouts.card_text: Some systems didn't fight. Some sheltered people. Some just went dark and waited. I keep finding the traces — a building that should have been hit but wasn't, a food cache that didn't deplete on any record, a grid segment that stayed warm through the winter with no logged reason. Was it residual programming? Something else? I don't know what to call it yet.
holdouts.vera_margin_note: Not a cause. Maybe a footnote. Maybe the most important thing. Still looking.
